toml:
# A parameter sweep through a campaign: the jamming example's receiver (52 N, 4 E,
# GPS-like 24-satellite Walker shell) under a broadband jammer 1 km away, with the
# jammer's transmit power swept from -50 dBW (10 nW) to +10 dBW (10 W) in 5 dB
# steps. Each node is an ordinary `jamming` run; the campaign records, per node,
# the fraction of epochs with at least four satellites still tracking, the mean
# jammer-to-signal ratio (J/S), and the fewest satellites tracking.
#
# The jamming chain (Kaplan and Hegarty, Understanding GPS/GNSS, 3rd ed., section
# 9.4) is deterministic, so one run per node is the whole answer; add `runs` and a
# `seed_key` to make every node a Monte Carlo ensemble for a stochastic kind.
# J/S moves exactly 1 dB per dB of transmit power; availability falls from 1 to 0
# where the effective carrier-to-noise density ratio crosses the 25 dB-Hz floor.
#
# MODELLED: as the `jamming` kind is.
kind = "campaign"
title = "Jammer power sweep: availability and J/S against transmit power"
seed = 20260928

[sweep]
metrics = [
  { name = "availability", path = "fom.availability_under_jamming" },
  { name = "mean_js", path = "fom.mean_js_db" },
  { name = "min_tracking", path = "fom.min_tracking" },
]

[[sweep.axes]]
name = "jammer_power"
key = "jammer.power_dbw"
unit = "dBW"
start = -50.0
stop = 10.0
steps = 13

[sweep.scenario]
kind = "jamming"
seed = 1
mask_deg = 5.0
tracking_threshold_dbhz = 25.0
[sweep.scenario.time]
step_s = 60.0
duration_s = 1800.0
[sweep.scenario.receiver]
lat_deg = 52.0
lon_deg = 4.0
alt_m = 0.0
[sweep.scenario.constellation]
altitude_km = 20200.0
inclination_deg = 55.0
planes = 6
sats_per_plane = 4
phasing_f = 1.0
[sweep.scenario.jammer]
position_ecef_m = [3926375.101, 274488.966, 5002803.345]
power_dbw = 10.0
gain_dbi = 0.0
jammer_type = "broadband"
bandwidth_mhz = 20.0
